newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases, diesel pressured by Med supplie.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases, diesel pressured by Med supplie.

text.p: NWE gas oil eased on Friday on weaker benchmark IPE futures with low sulphur diesel under particular pressure as Mediterranean supplies moved north, traders said.
They attributed some of the losses to falls in futures values -- June IPE gas oil settled $1.75 lower at $172.50 a tonne -- but said premiums had come under some pressure as well.
Lower sulphur diesel appeared to be the most fragile with fob Rotterdam barges done at June IPE $9.50 and $9.25.
An Algerian cargo was offered at June IPE +$9.0 cif Le Havre and +$9.50 cif Rotterdam.
The only bid heard was around June IPE +$8.0 cif NWE but traders said the complicated set of options attached to the bid made it virtually impossible to meet.

Heating oil was slightly firmer with steady demand for Swiss specification material and German demand expected to pick up after the weekend as many traders returned from Thursday's regional Corpus Christi holiday.
A Rotterdam refiner sold a Swiss spec barge for first half June delivery at June IPE +$2.25, while a parcel of ordinary 0.2 percent material was done at $1.25 fob ARA.
A 30,000 tonne Russian cargo was reported to have traded at June IPE +$1.0 cif NWE for first half June delivery.
